copy.headline: Paxton drops series of high-profile Texas lawsuits after election loss
copy.caption:
Cases involving gender-transition care, CAIR, ActBlue and other contentious issues have been dropped as a new Texas AG prepares to take office. After losing the election and preparing to hand the Texas Attorney General’s Office to an incoming Democrat, Attorney General Ken Paxton and his office have dropped a series of high-profile lawsuits.

The cases span some of the most politically charged issues Paxton’s office has pursued, including gender-transition care, transgender athletes, political fundraising, immigration advocacy and the Council on American-Islamic Relations.

story.title: Paxton drops series of high-profile Texas lawsuits after election loss
story.summary: Cases involving gender-transition care, CAIR, ActBlue and other contentious issues have been dropped as a new Texas AG prepares to take office. After losing the election and preparing to hand the Texas Attorney General’s Office to an incoming Democrat, Attorney General Ken Paxton and his office have dropped a series of high-profile lawsuits. The cases span some of the most politically charged issues Paxton’s office has pursued, including gender-transition care, transgender athletes, political fundraising, immigration advocacy and the Council on American-Islamic Relations. Among them is a February lawsuit asking a Collin County judge to declare CAIR a foreign terrorist organization. The group disputed the allegation throughout the lawsuit. Mustafaa Carroll of CAIR’s DFW chapter said a weight has been lifted and the organization looks forward to continuing to build trust between Muslims…
